brief.purpose: A dedicated kiln-dependent road surface with a visible movement advantage, distinct from structural red bricks.
brief.setting: Weathered late-nineteenth-century fired-clay street pavers, mainly charcoal-gray with muted oxide red and occasional tan.
brief.shape: Full cube, integrated native slab and stairs, and saw-cut pieces.
brief.fidelity_targets: A readable Minecraft-scale interpretation of late-19th-century vitrified-clay street paving: long, narrow and individually worn running-bond bricks in charcoal, gray, muted oxide red and umber. One 8-by-8-block painting supplies the world-aligned top face at 64 pixels per block; its own 64-pixel crop supplies sides and items.
brief.invariants: No road bonus on ordinary red brick or stone brick; no copied photo or Faithful pixels; no duplicate slab ecosystem.

reviews.finding: The seam-safe courses and color mix worked, but flat programmed fills made each paver bland.
Even with source swatches, 32 pixels forced too few pavers or too little individual surface detail, and the tan examples drew too much attention.
Ten courses carried the master's wear but made the pavers appear undersized in a one-meter Minecraft block.

Seven courses improved scale, but arbitrary brick-center crops lost the source's fired rims, mortar and surface wear. User play review found the pavers plain and stretched despite the earlier isolated visual pass.
Seven complete source courses retain worn rims, mottling and mortar at native size. Circular row offsets align at block boundaries; interior whole-face substitutions vary the broad road.
The first 8-by-8-block world-aligned mosaic removed per-block repetition but stamped the same source paver faces throughout the larger texture.
Every face was different, but the mechanically straight mortar still made the road feel like a grid.
Brick scale was much too large and a dark vignette made the image unsuitable for tiling.

reviews.stage: second whole-road image generation and material edit
reviews.finding: The one-image 8-by-8-block top is darker and has larger, more irregular pavers and richer individual wear. Photon/Faithful street-wide, close, and item views passed; a matching crop supplies sides and item faces. The image generator did not produce mathematically exact edge tiling, so long uninterrupted roads can still reveal the 8-block repeat.
